Story rail spacing [10235-203248]
column5: FIXED, MEASURED ON BOTH SIDES AT THREE BOARDS. FIGMA `Frame 1249` is a HORIZONTAL auto-layout whose LAST CHILD is the forward arrow, so the distance from the last tile to the arrow is the tile gap and not a value of its own. 1440 itemSpacing 20 with MIN alignment, and 6 x 91 + 6 x 20 + 36 = 702 closes the rail exactly; read on `10235:203248` AND on `10430:98331`, which agree child for child, so the 20 is two independent reads. 768 `11474:227168` is SPACE_BETWEEN in a fixed 708 and every one of its seven gaps resolves to 18: 7 x 78 + 7 x 18 + 36 = 708. 375 `11474:226917` and `11442:163929` are SPACE_BETWEEN in 343 and resolve to 4.75: 4 x 72 + 4 x 4.75 + 36 = 343. CODE BEFORE the scroller carried `gap-5` = 20 at every width and the row holding the arrow carried `gap-3` = 12 at every width, so at 1440 the arrow sat 12 from the rail against a drawn 20 (delta 8) and at 768 the tiles sat 20 apart against a drawn 18 (delta 2 per gap, 12 across six) with the arrow again at 12 against 18 (delta 6). ★ 12 IS NOT A MISREAD: it is the itemSpacing both redraws declare, and space-between overrides it at both, so it is an input the drawing never renders. CODE AFTER one `RAIL_GAP_CLASS` = `gap-[18px] xl:gap-5` on the scroller and on the row, resolving 18 below 1280 and 20 at and above it - 1440 delta 0/0, 768 delta 0/0. ONE DEPARTURE, STATED: the phone band keeps 18 rather than 4.75, because 4.75 is what four tiles leave in a fixed 343 and this rail scrolls instead of holding a width; the shipped 20 was not the drawn value there either. ORACLE StoryRail.figma.test.tsx, two new cases - one resolving the class at 375/639/641/767/768/769/1023/1279/1280/1440, one reading the gap off BOTH rendered elements and pinning that the arrow really is the row's second child. MUTATION-CHECKED four times, each alone and restored: gap-[18px] -> gap-[180px], xl:gap-5 -> xl:gap-50, `md:gap-3` added to the row, `md:gap-3` added to the scroller. The last two are the exact defect that shipped and both are EXTENDING - a substring check would have passed them.

column1: Bonding strip - NEW state [10235-202998]
column5: FIXED. THE CHIP DOES NOT RAMP AND THE ROW IT FILLS DOES NOT EITHER, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT SHIPPED. `icons/games` was read on all three boards - `10235:202999` (1440), `11442:164461` (768), `11442:163980` (375) - and is the SAME node value for value on each: a 40 x 18.182 chip at cornerRadius 3.636, filled #FFFFFF, holding a #001615 label whose ink measures 31.234 x 10.473 at (4.655, 4.073). Its row `Frame 654` is 18.182 tall on every board, gap 8, with the 10-tall bar filling from x=48 and NO right-hand label. CODE BEFORE one height ramp served both states - `h-[14px] md:h-[16px] xl:h-[18px]` - so the NEW row drew 14 at 375 against 18.18 (delta 4.18) and 16 at 768 against 18.18 (delta 2.18); the chip itself was `px-1.5 py-px` around a `text-[10px]/[14px]` label, i.e. sized to its own word at roughly 24 x 16 against a drawn 40 x 18.18. CODE AFTER the row takes `h-[18px]` in the NEW state and keeps the 14/16/18 ramp in the labelled one - which is correct, because there the height IS the label's line box - and the chip is `h-[18px] w-10` centred, radius 4 (against 3.636, delta 0.36), `bg-foreground` = #FFFFFF (index.css:477) on `text-background` = #001615 (:476), at 14/18. THE 10px LABEL IS RULED OUT BY THE INK ALONE and not by a font model: a cap height is always shorter than the em it is set in, so 10.473 of ink cannot come from a 10px face whatever the family. 14 is the step the rest of this card takes at its widest board and puts the ink within a pixel of the drawing. The chip is flattened to a vector, so its family, weight and tracking are NOT readable - `tracking-wide` (+2.5%) was the only positive tracking on this card and is now the -4% every measured label here carries; that one is stated as inherited, not measured. ORACLE PostCard.figma.test.tsx, three new cases, one of them the non-vacuity guard that `h-[14px]` is still reachable in the other state. MUTATION-CHECKED eight times, each alone and restored: h-[18px] -> h-[180px] on the row, h-[14px] -> h-[140px] on the labelled row, w-10 -> w-100, h-[18px] -> h-[180px] on the chip, rounded-[4px] -> rounded-[40px], bg-foreground -> md:bg-foreground, text-sm/[18px] -> text-sm/[180px], tracking -> md: variant, text-background -> md: variant, justify-center -> md:justify-center. Every one EXTENDING. ★ NO CARD ON TODAY'S FEED REACHES THIS BRANCH: `feedSource.ts:82` sets bonding to null on every mapped row, so this is the frame's spec made right for the day the data arrives, said plainly rather than left to be found.

column1: Discover header row [10235-203174]
column5: FIXED, AND THE HEADING BESIDE IT RE-MEASURED AND FOUND EXACT. FIGMA the row is `Frame 629` 1202 x 36 at 1440 (`10235:203174`), `Frame 630` 708 x 36 at 768 (`11442:164401`) and `Frame 630` 343 x 32 at 375 (`11442:163920`) - one step, at 768. CODE BEFORE `min-h-9`, a 36px floor at every width, so the phone row ran 4px tall against a drawn 32. CODE AFTER `min-h-8 md:min-h-9` - 375 delta 0, 768 delta 0, 1440 delta 0. It stays a MINIMUM rather than becoming `h-8`: `index.css:747-753` puts a 44px floor on every button at and below 768, the Create-new pill opts out with `no-min-size` and settles on its own 32/36, but a caller who drops a floored control in here gets a row that grows instead of one the control overflows by 8px. That reasoning is why the original was a minimum and it is unchanged; only the value was wrong. ALREADY MATCHED, both sides, on the same node: the heading is Manrope Light 300 at -4% and 20/24 (`11442:163925`), 24/28 (`11442:164406`), 32/36 (`10235:203179`); the code resolves `font-manrope font-light tracking-[-0.04em]` with `text-[20px]/[24px] md:text-[24px]/[28px] xl:text-[32px]/[36px]`, i.e. 20/24 below 768, 24/28 from 768 and 32/36 from 1280 - delta 0 on family, weight, tracking, size and leading at all three boards. ORACLE PostCard.figma.test.tsx, three new cases including one that asserts the row carries NO fixed height at any breakpoint, so the minimum cannot quietly become a maximum. MUTATION-CHECKED four times, each alone and restored: min-h-8 -> min-h-80, md:min-h-9 -> md:min-h-90, `h-9` added to the row, and text-[20px] -> text-[200px] on the heading. All RED, all EXTENDING.

column1: Comment preview - Show more [11529-291943]
column5: BUILT. IT IS ONE HALF OF A PAIR, AND THE OTHER HALF IS WHAT MAKES IT A SPEC RATHER THAN A DECORATION. FIGMA `11529:291943` is the last child of `Frame 355` (VERTICAL, gap 12) on `11442:163219`: y=56 under a 44-tall `Chat`, 343 wide, 14 tall, textAlignHorizontal LEFT, Manrope Regular 400 12/14 at -4%, fill #95A09F, visible. Where it is visible EXACTLY ONE `Chat` is, and its twin `11529:292026` on `11529:291953` - where three are - is hidden. So it is the collapsed state's affordance. CODE BEFORE the row did not exist: a grep for "Show more" across src/components/social returned only prose, against a positive control of one live node in Figma. CODE AFTER a button 12 under the preview stack, full width, left-aligned, `text-[#95A09F]`, carrying `no-min-size` because 14 is under the 44px floor that applies at and below 768 - the only width it is drawn at. It renders only while the post's count exceeds the previews on the card and only when there is a thread to open, and it opens THAT thread rather than expanding into a second source, so the row that says there is more and the control that shows it agree on where more is. An `Offline` count yields no row: an unread total is not a number of comments held back. ★ ONLY 375 DRAWS IT. A "Show more" search over `5100:183573`, `5101:186045`, `5194:271601` (1440) and `11442:164397` (768) returns ZERO against a positive control of one on `11442:163219`; those boards never draw a card in the collapsed state, so their silence is about the STATE and not about the control, and hiding it above 768 on that evidence would have been the guess. ITS TYPE IS THE PREVIEW ROW'S, extracted to `PREVIEW_ROW_CLASS` so the two cannot drift - at 375 the frame sets them identically (12/14, -4%) and only 375 draws the button, so the `md` step is INHERITED from the sibling, not read off a drawing. Stated in the code, in the test, and here. ORACLE PostCard.figma.test.tsx, five new cases; one asserts the button's type list EQUALS the preview row's rather than restating it, which is the claim actually being made. MUTATION-CHECKED eleven times, ten RED: leading -> [140px] and md: leading -> [160px], colour -> md: variant, text-left -> md: variant, w-full -> w-full-ish, no-min-size -> no-min-sized, the gate `> 0` -> `>= 0`, Math.max(0,..) -> Math.max(1,..), the click target -> a different id, and the stack's space-y-3 -> space-y-4. ONE EQUIVALENT MUTANT, named rather than hidden: replacing the `!isOffline(commentsCount)` guard with a truthy test still hides the row, because subtracting from an Offline object yields NaN and `NaN > 0` is false. The guard and the arithmetic refuse it independently; the mutant is equivalent, not a hole. ★ NOTHING REACHES THIS BRANCH TODAY either - `feedSource.ts:88` sets commentPreviews to [] on every mapped row, which the tripwire at src/components/social/showMoreComments.unavailable.test.ts still asserts. That file's prose said no such row existed; it now says where the row is, because a stale paragraph would have told the next reader a built control was not built.

column5: GEOMETRY AND TYPE RE-MEASURED ON BOTH SIDES AT THREE BOARDS AND FOUND EXACT; THE RING COLOUR IS THE ONE OPEN AXIS AND IT NEEDS A RULING, NOT A GUESS. Caption width 72 / 78 / 90 against `w-[72px] md:w-[78px] xl:w-[90px]` - delta 0/0/0. Caption type Manrope Regular 400 12/14 at 375 and 12/16 at 768 AND at 1440, letter-spacing -4%, fill #FFFFFF; the code resolves `text-xs/[14px] md:text-xs/[16px] tracking-[-0.04em] text-foreground` with the family inherited from the body's `font-sans`, which is Manrope (design-tokens.ts:352) and is not overridden here because the caption is a span and not a heading - delta 0 on family, size, leading, tracking and colour at all three. Arrow 36 square at y=24 / 29 / 34, which is (rail - 36) / 2 on each board, against `h-9 w-9 mt-[24px] md:mt-[29px] xl:mt-[34px]` - delta 0/0/0. THE OPEN AXIS the ring stroke is one of THREE accents, not two: across seventeen tiles at three boards the strokes read #17F9B4, #FF7E50 and #56C7F3, and the colour follows the CREATOR rather than the position - @CryptosTraderX is #17F9B4 on all three boards, @CryptoWhizKid and @BlockchainGuru and @AltcoinAdventurer are #FF7E50, @TokenMasterX and @DigiCoinExpert are #56C7F3. The code models two states and paints `border-primary` (#2DEDAD) and `border-border` (#123F3C), and NEITHER hex appears on any tile of any board. So both states are wrong today and the mapping cannot be read off the boards. Escalated with two options rather than guessed; see the lane report.
